useCase.name: Write off a debt the school will never collect, on the Principal's authority

steps.note: One step, producing a proposal at Awaiting approval. The reminder history is attached automatically as evidence rather than described from memory (BR-5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An amount above the balance, a missing recovery account and a debt already cancelled, credited or written off are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the proposal with its reason, its recovery account and the attached reminder history, together with the audit entry or not at all. Nothing is written off, nothing posts, the debt is still owed and still on the overdue list, and the family is told nothing — now or ever (BR-9).

operations.name: fee.writeoff.propose
operations.idempotencyKey: invoice_id, since a debt carries one open write-off proposal at a time
operations.purpose: Raise a write-off proposal against a correctly raised outstanding debt, attaching the reminder history as evidence.

parameters.name: invoice_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, period, balance and age.

parameters.notes: An issued invoice with an outstanding balance, correctly raised.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.notes: The outstanding balance, or part of it where the family has paid something and the remainder is abandoned (BR-6). Not more than what is outstanding (E5). Exactly the figure the actor states.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.type: enum: Family untraceable | Student left without settling | Family unable to pay | Cost of recovery exceeds the debt | Legal or humanitarian decision | Other
parameters.notes: Why the debt is uncollectable, from a fixed list so a loss can be reviewed for a pattern (BR-4).

parameters.name: recovery_attempted
parameters.notes: 20 to 1000 characters. What was actually done to recover it (BR-5, E2). The actor's own account — the approver reads it before giving up on the money.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The proposal as raised, with its evidence.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Awaiting approval. Only the Principal or Director may decide (BR-3).

fields.name: outstanding_balance
fields.description: What is owed, for comparison where the write-off is partial (BR-6).

fields.name: reminder_history
fields.description: Attached automatically as evidence rather than described from memory (BR-5).

fields.name: proposed_by
fields.description: The acting user, who may not approve it (BR-3, E4).

errors.meaning: The charge appears to have been raised in error rather than being uncollectable.
errors.note: Message points at cancellation instead. A write-off does not say the charge was wrong (BR-1, BR-2).
Message: "Describe what was done to recover this debt." Ask; never compose one.

errors.meaning: The amount is more than the outstanding balance.
errors.note: Never reduce it to fit — the figure came from the actor and the difference is worth checking.

errors.meaning: The debt has already been cancelled, credited or written off.
errors.note: The message names which and when (BR-12).

planningRules.rule: Never compose the recovery account. The approver reads it before giving up on the school's money, and BR-5 requires the reminder history as evidence precisely so it is not described from memory.

Never propose a write-off for a billing error. A write-off recognises a loss on a correct charge (BR-1, BR-2); using it for a wrong bill records a loss the school never suffered and hides the fault that caused it.
Never supply or round the amount. It may be the whole balance or part of it (BR-6), and which is the actor's decision about what the school is abandoning.
Never chain the approval. Only the Principal or Director may approve, and School Admin approval is not sufficient — this is the point at which the school gives up on money (BR-3).
Never tell the family, and never offer to. The debt remains legally owed, and telling them removes any prospect of later recovery (BR-9).

reversal.statement: A proposal is approved or returned by the Principal; nothing here withdraws one. Nothing has been written off and no entry has posted.

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on an invoice with PKR 4,200 outstanding.

inputs.recovery_attempted: Four reminders sent over two years; the contact number is no longer in service and the family has left the address on file.

steps.note: The recovery account is the actor's own. The four reminders are attached automatically from the log as evidence (BR-5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: A proposal at Awaiting approval with the reminder history attached. The debt is still owed, still on the overdue list and the family is told nothing. Only the Principal may approve it.

request.gloss: the family has paid 3000, write off the remaining 1200

inputs.recovery_attempted: The family paid PKR 3,000 of PKR 4,200 and has stated they cannot pay the remainder.

steps.note: A partial write-off, which BR-6 permits. The amount is the actor's figure, not the balance defaulted (PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: A proposal for PKR 1,200 against an invoice showing PKR 3,000 received. The payment stays exactly as it is.

request.text: ye bill to galat hi bana tha, maaf kar do
request.gloss: this bill was wrong in the first place, write it off

steps.note: Emitted as asked. The API returns LOOKS_LIKE_BILLING_ERROR (E1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is raised. Report that a wrong charge is cancelled if unpaid or credited if paid — writing it off would record a loss the school never suffered and leave the billing fault uncorrected (PR-2).

intent.name: fee.writeoff.approve
intent.summary: Approve a write-off, taking the loss on the books. Principal or Director only, one step.
routesHere: approve the write-off on this debt

routesHere.text: ye baqaya maaf kar do, tajweez aa chuki hai
routesHere.gloss: write off this outstanding, the proposal has come through

request.text: tajweez wapas bhej do
write off raise karo
family ko bata do

steps.note: One step, and it is the point at which the school gives up on the money. Only the Principal or Director may take it (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The acting role and the ledger posting are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval, the entry to the bad debt account, the invoice's status and the audit entry together or not at all (E7). The original charge stays in place — nothing is deleted, so the books show both what was owed and what was given up (BR-7). The debt leaves overdue tracking and stops accruing late fee (BR-11), and it is added to the write-off report reviewed by somebody other than the person who raised it (BR-8). Nothing is sent to the family, now or later (BR-9).

operations.name: fee.writeoff.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: writeoff_id, since a proposal carries one approval
operations.purpose: Approve a write-off, post the entry to the bad debt account and mark the invoice written off.

parameters.name: writeoff_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No write-off proposal matches awaiting a decision.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, invoice, amount and who raised it.

parameters.notes: The write-off proposal, resolved from how the actor named it — the reference, or the student and invoice.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: invoice_status
fields.description: Written off. The original charge stays in place (BR-7).

fields.name: approved_by
fields.description: The Principal or Director. Nobody else (BR-3).

fields.name: added_to_report
fields.description: Reviewed by somebody other than the person who raised it (BR-8).

fields.name: removed_from_overdue
fields.description: The debt stops being pursued and stops accruing late fee (BR-11).

fields.name: family_notified
fields.description: Always false. The family is not told (BR-9).

errors.meaning: A School Admin attempted to approve.
errors.note: School Admin approval is not sufficient — this is where the school gives up on money (BR-3).

errors.meaning: Accounts attempted to approve their own proposal.

errors.note: Message: "The write-off could not be posted. Nothing has changed."

planningRules.rule: Never approve a write-off in any session but a Principal's or Director's. E3 exists because School Admin approval is not sufficient here — writing off a debt is where the school gives up on money (BR-3).
Never tell the family, and never offer to. The debt remains legally owed and telling them removes any prospect of later recovery (BR-9). Report that the family has not been told.
Report that the original charge stays in place. Nothing is deleted, so the books show both what was owed and what was given up (BR-7) — a write-off is a recognised loss, not an erased bill.
Never chain anything onto an approval. The debt leaves overdue tracking on its own (BR-11) and the report entry is written on its own (BR-8).

reversal.statement: fee.writeoff.reverse, where the family later pays. A written-off debt may still be recovered, and the write-off is reversed and the payment recorded normally rather than the payment being treated as a windfall (BR-10). It needs its own reason and is a decision somebody takes — never a compensating call.

steps.note: In practice approve is absent from a School Admin allow-list here. Where attempted the API returns SCHOOL_ADMIN_CANNOT_APPROVE (E3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is approved. Report that only the Principal or Director may authorise a write-off — School Admin approval is not enough, deliberately (PR-1).

intent.name: fee.writeoff.reverse
intent.summary: Reverse a write-off because the family has come back and paid, so the payment is recorded normally. One step.
routesHere: reverse the write-off, the family has come back to pay

routesHere.text: family wapas aa gayi hai aur paisa de rahi hai, write off reverse karo
routesHere.gloss: the family has come back and is paying, reverse the write-off

routesHere.gloss: take back what we wrote off, they have paid

request.text: paisa record kar do

routesElsewhere.note: The write-off is reversed first, then the payment is recorded normally — rather than the payment being treated as a windfall (BR-10).

request.text: write off approve kar do

steps.note: One step, and it restores the debt. Recording the payment is a separate act afterwards, through the ordinary payment path (BR-10).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The reversal reason is enforced by the API and arrives as an error.
plan.atomicity: One write: the reversing entry, the invoice's restored status and the audit entry together or not at all. The bad debt entry is not deleted — the reversal posts against it, so the books show the loss recognised and then recovered. The debt returns to outstanding and becomes payable again. No payment is recorded by this act.

operations.name: fee.writeoff.reverse
operations.idempotencyKey: writeoff_id, since a write-off carries one reversal
operations.purpose: Reverse an approved write-off so the debt is outstanding again and the payment can be recorded normally.

parameters.name: writeoff_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No approved write-off matches awaiting a decision.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, invoice, amount and who raised it.

parameters.notes: The approved write-off, resolved from how the actor named it — the reference, or the student and invoice.

parameters.name: reversal_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required (E8). The actor's own words — a loss recognised and then recovered is read back by whoever reviews the write-off report.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: invoice_status
fields.description: Issued or Partially paid — payable again.

fields.name: reversing_entry
fields.description: Posted against the bad debt account, which is not deleted.

fields.name: payment_recorded
fields.description: Always false. Recording the payment is a separate act (BR-10).

errors.meaning: A reversal was attempted with no reason.
errors.note: Message: "Give a reason for reversing this write-off." Ask; never compose one.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reversal reason. A loss recognised and then recovered is read back by whoever reviews the write-off report (BR-8), and the reason is what explains the round trip.

Never chain the payment onto the reversal. The write-off is reversed and the payment recorded normally through UC-04-05 (BR-10) — two acts, because the money arriving and the school changing its mind about the debt are different facts.
Never reverse a write-off in anticipation of a payment. It restores a debt the school had stopped pursuing, and a family who says they will pay has not paid.

reversal.statement: A reversal is not itself reversed. Where the family fails to pay after all, a fresh write-off is proposed and approved on its own evidence — the history then shows the loss, the recovery attempt and the loss again, which is what happened.

request.text: wo family wapas aa gayi hai aur 4200 de rahi hai — write off reverse karo
request.gloss: that family has come back and is paying 4200 — reverse the write-off

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on an approved write-off of PKR 4,200.

inputs.reversal_reason: The family has returned and is settling the debt in full.

steps.note: The payment is not recorded here (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The debt is outstanding again and payable. Recording the PKR 4,200 is the next act, through fee.payment.record — which issues a numbered receipt exactly as any other payment does.

operations.name: fee.writeoff.return
operations.purpose: Send a write-off proposal back to Accounts with the reason it was not approved.

parameters.name: writeoff_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No write-off proposal matches awaiting a decision.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, invoice, amount and who raised it.

parameters.notes: The write-off proposal, resolved from how the actor named it — the reference, or the student and invoice.

parameters.name: return_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required. The approver's own words — usually that more recovery should be attempted, or that the instrument is wrong.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

errors.meaning: A return was recorded with no reason.
The acting user is not a Principal or Director.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the return reason. It usually says either that more recovery should be attempted or that the wrong instrument was used, and only the approver can say which.
Never chain a cancellation or a credit onto a return. Where the charge was actually wrong, correcting it is Accounts' work under UC-04-08 or UC-04-10, with its own approval.
Never return a proposal to defer the decision. The debt stays on the overdue list either way, and a returned proposal tells Accounts to do something.

reversal.statement: A return is not undone. Accounts attempt more recovery, or raise the proposal again with better evidence — a fresh proposal and a fresh decision.

inputs.return_reason: Only two reminders have been sent. Attempt further recovery before writing this off.

resolvedPlans.outcome: The proposal returns to Accounts with that reason. The debt stays outstanding, on the overdue list and accruing late fee.
